title: Patna and Nanded
hookLine: he funded buildings at the Tenth Guru's birthplace and resting place

cards: Draw a line on a map of India. Start at Patna, on the Ganges, far to the east. Follow it a long way south and west, down into the Deccan, to Nanded, on the Godavari river.
Neither city was in Ranjit Singh's kingdom. Yet his money went to both, to build and adorn places Sikhs travel to. One is where the Tenth Guru was born.
The other is where his earthly life ended.

teach.h: PATNA, WHERE THE TENTH GURU WAS BORN.
teach.b: Guru Gobind Singh was born at Patna, while his father, Guru Tegh Bahadur, was traveling in the east, and he spent his early years there before the family came to Anandpur.
The place of his birth became a gurdwara, and today it's one of the Takhts, the seats of authority Sikhs honor.

teach.h: NANDED, WHERE HIS EARTHLY LIFE ENDED.
teach.b: At the end of his life, Guru Gobind Singh traveled south to the Deccan, and at Nanded he gave the Guruship to the Granth and left this world. Sikhs call the gurdwara there Hazur Sahib, and it too is a Takht.
Histories and gurdwara tradition say Ranjit Singh sent money and craftsmen to both places, to raise and beautify the buildings. He had already covered the Harmandir in gold, inside his own kingdom.
These gifts went far beyond his borders, to places he would never rule, and that's the point of them. They weren't about holding land; they were about honoring the Guru.

teach.h: A LINE FROM THE GANGES TO THE GODAVARI.
teach.b: The Tenth Guru's life ran from the Ganges to the Godavari, and a Maharaja in Lahore sent his gifts along that same line, east and south.
Sikhs still travel it today, and tradition says some of what they see there was paid for from Lahore.

how: Sikhs travel to Takht Sri Patna Sahib and Takht Sri Hazur Sahib at Nanded, the places of Guru Gobind Singh's birth and his final days, and give donations there.

o: a seat of authority that Sikhs honor

s: Patna and Nanded were inside Ranjit Singh's kingdom
both were far outside it; the gifts went beyond his borders.
Guru Gobind Singh gave the Guruship to the Granth at Nanded
it was there, at the end of his life, that he passed it to the Granth.
the Tenth Guru was born in the Punjab
he was born in Patna, on the Ganges, while Guru Tegh Bahadur was traveling in the east.

games.q: you rule the Punjab. the Tenth Guru's birthplace and resting place are in lands you will never rule. what do you do?
o: send money and craftsmen to build and adorn them.
try to bring those cities into your kingdom.
games.why: histories and gurdwara tradition say he sent gifts to both, honoring the Guru rather than seeking land.

practice: Bring to mind a place that's holy to you or to someone you love: a gurdwara, a church, a temple, a grave, a tree, a kitchen where someone prayed.
Picture it clearly, and choose one small gift it could use, flowers, an hour of cleaning, a word of thanks to whoever keeps it. If you pray, you can say Waheguru on each breath out.

wordCard.voice: Takht, a seat of authority Sikhs honor; Patna and Nanded, the Tenth Guru's birthplace and resting place, are both Takhts, far from Lahore yet both honored with the Maharaja's gifts.

orig.note: takht, throne or seat; Patna Sahib and Hazur Sahib are both Takhts.

carryVoice: Your line: gifts to the guru's places. Some gifts are about honor, not land. Until tomorrow.
